name: DOSUE-RR
full_name: Dark-(photon dark)-matter Observing System for Un-Explored Radio-Range
summary: Kyoto University applies low-noise millimeter-wave technology to dark-photon dark matter, developing receivers for several frequency bands and shielded cryogenic systems.
detection_principle: Dark photons convert to millimeter waves at a metal surface; antennas, cryogenic receivers and shielding suppress thermal backgrounds and radio interference.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: 2023 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for Dark Photon Dark Matter in the Mass Range 41–74 μeV using Millimeter-Wave Receiver and Radioshielding Box

collaboration.name: DOSUE-RR Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Published dark-photon kinetic-mixing limits; upgrades to different bands belong to the same series and are not counted separately.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
